connection.notes: Use the shared pooler: session mode (port 5432) for workers and checks, transaction mode (port 6543) for short request traffic. Pooler usernames are <role>.<project-ref>. The Supabase REST/GraphQL Data API, the secret (service-role) key and the postgres role are never used by adapters.

roles.read: Dedicated login created with SQL (CREATE ROLE ... LOGIN), granted SELECT on the catalog tables only. Projects that enable RLS with no policies (as Storefront A's lock-down does) also need a SELECT policy for this role on each catalog table, or it sees zero rows. See docs/runbooks/read-only-role.md.
roles.write: Dedicated Postgres role with INSERT and UPDATE on the profile's write tables only. Phase 3, server-side only.
roles.never: The secret (service-role) key, the postgres role, or any role with BYPASSRLS.

isolation.row_level_security: Storefront A enables RLS on every public table with no policies and revokes all privileges from anon/authenticated, which shuts the Data API off. Commerce OS roles get narrow per-table policies; they are never granted BYPASSRLS.

assets.store: Supabase Storage. Storefront A: private bucket `artwork`; storage.objects has RLS on with no policies.
assets.reference_format: Storefront A: `/objects/uploads/<id>` in the database, served by the app server.
assets.upload: Storefront A: the app server writes the object and a visibility record at `_meta/<object path>.json` in the same bucket, using the secret key. A Commerce OS upload must go through the app's own upload flow or reproduce both writes with a separately scoped credential; decided in Phase 3.

schema_changes: Storefront A: only through drizzle migration files in its git repository (no automatic changes on publish), re-running its RLS lock-down after new tables. Mappings are still bound to a schema fingerprint, checked at Gate 4.
verify_before_use: Session-pooler connection as <role>.<project-ref> for the Commerce OS read role.
Whether a role VALID UNTIL date is set: an expired role fails pooler auth with EAUTHQUERY.
Storage upload authorization that never uses the secret (service-role) key in Commerce OS.
